newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH PAPER UNION HEAD SEES PAY RISE PRESSURES.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH PAPER UNION HEAD SEES PAY RISE PRESSURES.

text.p: There will be more pressure for wage increases in the next round of incomes settlement talks due late next autum, Jarmo Lahteenmaki, chairman of the Paper Workers' Union, said on Friday.

In an interview with Reuters at the council meeting of the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK), Lahteenmaki said the fact that there will be no nominal pay rises in 1997 will up pressures in the coming round of wage talks.
"The situation will surely be more tense than it was in the autumn of 1995," he said, referring to negotiations leading to the current two-year nationwide settlement.
But he said it was still too early to say anything about the form of the coming talks, whether they would be centralised aiming for a national deal or decentralised sector by sector.

"We must first see how the current ... deal has worked," he said. "In the paper industry we were prepared for solidarity in the name of (improved) employment ... but it does no seem to have worked very well," he added.
On EMU, Lahteenmaki said he agreed with SAK's demands for funds as buffers against fluctuations, and he put his hopes in talks with employers and the government on a national framework for EMU.
"These talks will of course not be easy ... but the targets are serious for the unions", he said.
The paper workers, like the SAK, have not yet defined a final a stance on EMU but Lahteenmaki repeated an earlier statment that his union is critical to the project.
